source:
Kai: The ranking is bogus because the survey sample was self-selected.
Mia: The ranking should stand; self-selection biases it less than you think.
Kai: Suppose I grant the sample. I would still call the ranking bogus.

positions.label: The ranking is bogus
positions.thesis: The ranking is bogus because the survey sample was self-selected.
positions.steelman: Self-selected samples overrepresent the motivated, which can manufacture any ranking.

groundingQuotes.quote: The ranking is bogus because the survey sample was self-selected.

positions.label: The ranking should stand
positions.thesis: The ranking should stand; self-selection biases it less than Kai thinks.
positions.steelman: Modest self-selection bias does not overturn an ordering that is robust across methods.

groundingQuotes.quote: The ranking should stand; self-selection biases it less than you think.

claims.statement: Self-selection biases the ranking less than critics think.

groundingQuotes.quote: self-selection biases it less than you think

disagreementCandidates.question: Does self-selection make the ranking bogus?
disagreementCandidates.summary: Kai says the sample invalidates the ranking; Mia says the bias is small.
disagreementCandidates.resolutionCondition: A probability sample run alongside the self-selected one.

claimStakeCandidates.consequence: Kai says he would still call the ranking bogus even if he granted the sample, and the source states no other reason for that verdict.

groundingQuotes.quote: Suppose I grant the sample. I would still call the ranking bogus.

caveats: The sample's composition is asserted by one side and conceded for argument only.
